name: Fake output hashes and keys
summary: Counts outputs whose hash or key is data as data carrier bytes
catches: Data hidden in the hashes and keys of outputs. A real hash or x-only key looks random, so one byte value eight times in a program, a run of six identical bytes, or a taproot key that is not on the curve marks it as data, along with its same-type, same-value siblings. Three or more P2WSH outputs sharing one value of 546 sat or less also count: file encoders pay every chunk the same dust amount.
passes: Payments to every address type, batched payments and pool payouts. The all-zero burn hash used by Stacks block commits is exempt.

example.note: an ACME file, a run of P2WSH outputs at the 330 sat dust floor whose programs hold a compressed HTML file

name: Dead conditional branches
summary: Counts data in a conditional branch that constants make unreachable
catches: Data placed in a branch of a script that can never run because a constant decides the condition, such as `OP_1 OP_NOTIF <data> OP_ENDIF` or the dead side of an `OP_ELSE`. Knots already counts the `OP_FALSE OP_IF` envelope; this catches the other constant-decided forms.
passes: Branches decided by a signature or a witness value, which is how real spending conditions branch: Lightning, timelocks, multisig recovery paths. Those are never counted.

example.note: a 37 KB JPEG XL image in an `OP_1 OP_NOTIF` branch

name: Bare data envelopes
summary: Counts a run of pushes ended by OP_DROP or OP_2DROP as data carrier bytes
catches: A run of data pushes dropped again with `OP_DROP` or `OP_2DROP`, the envelope shape inscriptions use when `OP_IF` is not available. The whole run counts as data, not only the last push.
passes: Scripts that drop the result of an opcode, such as `<n> OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY OP_DROP` in timelocks. Only pushes followed by a drop count.

example.note: an 87 KB JPEG inscription in an ord envelope ended by `OP_2DROP`

name: Fake multisig keys
summary: Counts the keys of a multisig that no signature in the spend proves, beyond 10 per script, as data carrier bytes
catches: File chunks dressed as public keys: a 1-of-15 multisig where one key signs and the other 14 each carry 31 bytes of a file. Keys that no signature in the spend can prove, beyond ten per script, count as data. Covers P2WSH, P2SH and tapscript `multi_a`.
passes: Real multisig and vaults, which since the fork leave at most ten keys unsigned in a script (a 2-of-3 vault with timelocked recovery branches; a plain 2-of-3 leaves one), including federations spending 11-of-15.
cost: A Liquid federation spend through its 2-of-3 emergency branch leaves 16 keys unsigned and is refused. There has been one since the fork, `97f7d78b0b9ad4d47e150659c3091d905c3565fe7e6fd8977e4326b2b7af2270` at block 963410. Other nodes and miners still carry it.

example.note: a file in 475 inputs at 546 sat each, 474 of them a 1-of-15 multisig whose 14 unused keys are file chunks

name: Token messages
summary: Refuses an OP_RETURN that holds a JSON token message or an Omni Layer message
catches: Token operations written into an `OP_RETURN` that `-rejecttokens` does not match. A JSON object whose `"p"` field names the protocol is the BRC-20 format, which ico-20, crc-20 and others copy: `{"p":"ico-20","op":"mint","tick":"LEAF"}`. Omni Layer messages begin with `omni`. Most JSON mints on this chain are 41 or 42 bytes, under even a 42-byte `-datacarriersize`.
passes: Every other `OP_RETURN`: swap and bridge memos, Stacks block commits, Babylon staking, and random data that happens to start with `{`. The payload has to start as a JSON object with a top-level `"p"` member whose value is a string.

example.note: the first ico-20 mint since the fork, `{"p":"ico-20","op":"mint","tick":"LEAF"}` in a 42-byte `OP_RETURN`
